prompt:
Write a police officer's crash report narrative (about 150 words). Collision type: side impact at intersection in Houston, Texas. The claimant was a passenger and reported neck and back strain. Refer to people as Driver 1, Driver 2 or Passenger. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1063; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- It is not clear whether all of the damage came from this impact.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- A few old scratches may be older than this crash.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text: Officers responded to a report of a two-vehicle collision at a signalized intersection in Houston, Texas. Driver 1 stated that the vehicle was struck on the driver's side by Driver 2, who entered the intersection against the signal. Driver 2 acknowledged the approach and did not dispute how the collision occurred. Photographs taken at the scene and statements from two independent witnesses are consistent with that account, and both witnesses described the impact as sudden and forceful. Driver 1 is the named insured on the policy for the vehicle involved. A passenger, identified only as Passenger, was seated in the front right position and was confirmed present by officers and both witnesses. Passenger reported neck and back strain at the scene and was transported for evaluation. It is not yet clear whether these injuries resulted from this collision, as no medical findings had been made at the time of this report. Officers noted a few older scratches on the rear quarter panel that may predate this crash, and it is not clear whether all of the visible damage resulted from this impact. Further assessment is recommended.
